1	# Spec: Spec-driven HFSS agent — robustness and token efficiency from one change of artifact
2	
3	Status: needs-triage
4	Feature: hfss-agent-spec-driven
5	
6	## Problem Statement
7	
8	Two runs and one pilot have now measured the tool. The baseline (`silent-engine`)
9	cost 398,130 tokens / 424 parts / ~1.6 h. The post-refactor pilot
10	(`shiny-canyon`) cost 1,579,333 tokens / 1,392 parts / 25 h and returned
11	**NO-GO on all three acceptance axes** (`.scratch/hfss-agent-perf-refactor/pilot-retrospective.md`).
12	
13	The perf refactor was not wrong — its instrumentation is what caught the
14	regression, and its doctrines (phase sessions, State ledger, Verification
15	line, idempotent stages, detached watchdog) are sound and are **kept in
16	full** by this spec. But it optimized the containment machinery around a
17	decision that was never revisited: **the agent's primary output artifact is
18	free-form Python.**
19	
20	Every expensive mechanism in the current design exists to contain the blast
21	radius of that one choice:
22	
23	- the `py_compile`/import static gate exists because generated code may not parse;
24	- the `PASS:` Verification line exists because a run's success is otherwise unknowable;
25	- ADR 0008 idempotency is a *discipline* the model must remember per script;
26	- read-back sync needs `capture_state.py` + `12_verify_sync.py` replaying eight
27	  scripts on a port-pinned second desktop (36 steps in baseline; 6 replays × ~8 min
28	  in the pilot) because the scripts and the live model can silently diverge;
29	- the 4,376-file KB exists so the model can look up call signatures it would
30	  not need if the surface were typed (~20 discovery steps in baseline).
31	
32	Three further findings sharpen the case:
33	
34	1. **The safety machinery is currently decorative.** `confirm_solve.terminal_status()`
35	   returns `None` on **9 of 9** real profiles on this box — its regex omits the
36	   escaped quotes AEDT actually writes (`\'Status\', \'Normal Completion\'`). So
37	   `ws_common.guard_verdict()`

1	# 06 — Main-loop model experiment: the cheapest test of the most expensive assumption
2	
3	**What to build:** Re-run the pilot's problem class with the main loop on a
4	capable reasoning model, changing nothing else, and record the run card. The
5	perf refactor's decision 7 pinned `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` at `variant: low` on
6	the reasoning that the model was not the cost driver. The pilot then spent
7	1,579,333 tokens — 4× the baseline — and the retrospective's own breakdown
8	attributes the bulk to capability failures rather than ceremony failures: five
9	solve submissions where one was correct, eight readout shapes tried in
10	succession, a guessed `EXPECTED_SD` that could not have been right, and
11	process-detach churn. Foam-Agent's ablation is the external evidence: identical
12	harness, 88.2% success on Claude 3.5 Sonnet versus 59.1% on GPT-4o — a larger
13	swing than their entire retrieval improvement. Ticket 08 of the perf refactor
14	already built the single swap point, so this is a config change plus one run.
15	Sequenced deliberately **before** the architecture work: it is the cheapest
16	experiment with the largest expected effect, and a strong result changes how much
17	of phases 2–4 is worth building.
18	
19	**Blocked by:** 01, 02 (banking and stage detection must work or the run is
20	unmeasurable), 04 (the metric), 05 (a vetted case to run).
21	
22	**Status:** ready-for-human
23	
24	- [ ] Main loop repointed via the existing provider alias; subagents left on the cheap tier
25	- [ ] One greenfield run on a vetted canonical case, same ceremony, nothing else changed
26	- [ ] Run card records tokens, parts, wall time, outcome, escape-hatch count, and cost per completed simulation against both prior baselines
27	- [ ] Retrospective note: which of the pilot's five cost centres shrank, and which did not — the ones that did not are the true architecture problems and should be cited in the phase-2 go/no-go
28	- [ ] Explicit go/no-go recommendation on phases 2–4 written into this ticket's Comments
29

1	# 05 — Canonical case set: end N=1 acceptance
2	
3	**What to build:** A regression set of five canonical structures, so that
4	acceptance stops being a single pilot whose failure modes cannot be
5	disentangled. The `shiny-canyon` NO-GO is the argument: with N=1 there is no way
6	to separate "the refactor regressed" from "this paper's geometry was internally
7	inconsistent" from "the readout path was broken" — and the retrospective shows
8	all three tangled together. Published comparators run 110 cases (Foam-Agent) and
9	315 (ChatCFD); five is not that, but five is enough to localise a regression.
10	Choose for coverage of the Spine rather than variety of physics: **inset-fed
11	rectangular patch** (the original Proof-1 recipe), **bowtie** (the measured
12	baseline, so history is comparable), **microstrip line** (trivial geometry,
13	exercises ports and Z0 — the fastest Tier 1 case), **coupled-line filter**
14	(multi-object geometry, multiple ports), **horn** (swept/lofted geometry, the
15	schema's hardest shape). Each case is a directory holding its source recipe
16	notes, its expected key dimensions, its QA signals, and — once ticket 07 lands —
17	its `design.yaml`. Until then they are fixture data and Tier 1 build targets.
18	
19	**Blocked by:** None. Becomes far more useful after 07/10, but the cases can be
20	written now and are needed to scope the schema honestly.
21	
22	**Status:** ready-for-human
23	
24	- [x] Five case directories under `knowledge/cases/`, each with recipe source, key dimensions, target quantity, and QA signals
25	- [x] Every dimension traceable to a vetted source (textbook or self-consistent paper); the Astuti bowtie is explicitly excluded or annotated as the known-inconsistent case
26	- [x] At least one case is deliberately cheap enough for routine Tier 1 runs (microstrip line)
27	- [x] The horn case is written even though the schema will not cover it at v1 — it is the scope pressure that keeps the schema honest
28	- [x] Cases referenced from the spec's testing section and from `verify

1	# 04 — Cost per completed simulation, and the three-tier test harness
2	
3	**What to build:** Two measurement changes that make every later decision
4	legible. First, the run card's headline metric becomes **cost per successfully
5	completed simulation**, not tokens per run — a run that burns 1.58 M tokens and
6	delivers no readable result must score worse than one that burns 400 k and
7	delivers, and today's metric cannot express that. Extend `scripts/run_card.py`
8	with an outcome field (`completed` / `escalated` / `abandoned`), the escape-hatch
9	stage-script count, and a derived cost-per-completion; keep the existing token /
10	parts / wall-time columns so the `silent-engine` and `shiny-canyon` history stays
11	comparable. Second, split verification into three tiers so that "did I break it"
12	stops requiring license-hours: **Tier 0** offline (schema, references, units,
13	physics pre-check, parsers against `fixtures/real/`, compiler golden tests) in
14	seconds with no AEDT; **Tier 1** build-only on a live desktop through
15	`validate_simple()` and snapshot capture, no solve; **Tier 2** full end-to-end
16	including solve, readout, and QA. One runner script per tier, each printing a
17	single machine-parseable summary line in the established `PASS:` house style.
18	
19	**Blocked by:** None. Land the harness before the architecture work so its
20	effect is measurable.
21	
22	**Status:** ready-for-human
23	
24	- [x] Run card records outcome, escape-hatch count, and cost per completed simulation; existing baselines re-scored under the new metric with the re-scoring documented
25	- [x] `scripts/tier0.py` runs with no AEDT installed and no license, in under ~30 s
26	- [ ] `scripts/tier1.py` builds a named canonical spec on a live desktop and captures its snapshot without solving
27	- [x] Each tier prints exactly one summary line; no tier dumps pyAEDT INFO logs into stdout
28	- [x] `verify_skill.py` extended to assert the tier scripts and the metric exist
29	- [x] Tier 0 wired into the template README as the pre-f

1	# Pilot retrospective — ticket 06 (acceptance gate) breakdown & corrective plan
2	
3	Written 2026-08-06, immediately after the user terminated the test at the
4	corrected-geometry QA read. Applies to the `shiny-canyon` pilot session.
5	
6	## Verdict
7	
8	**NO-GO on all three acceptance axes.** The user terminated the pilot at the
9	results-readout step (which never worked), after a paper-consistency
10	discovery: Astuti et al. 2022's bow-tie dimensions are internally
11	inconsistent (the authors' equations do not reproduce their Table I / Fig 1;
12	their real patch was ~2*26.32 base with ~26.32 sides).
13	
14	| Metric | baseline silent-engine | pilot shiny-canyon | vs baseline | threshold | verdict |
15	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
16	| billed tokens | 398,130 | 1,579,333 | **+297%** | ≥50% lower | FAIL |
17	| parts | 424 | 1,392 | **+228%** | ≥40% lower | FAIL |
18	| wall time | ~1.6 h | 25 h 1 min | **+1463%** | ≥40% lower | FAIL |
19	
20	Wall time includes ~21 h idle between the solve-3 completion and the user's
21	return; even excluding that gap the session ran ~4 h of active work versus
22	~1.6 h baseline. The refactor's own instrumentation did its job: the run
23	card caught a regression the ceremony should have prevented.
24	
25	## What the ceremony did right (fair accounting)
26	
27	- Clarification → ledger: one locked parameter set, one correction
28	  (the Fig-1 L/W reading) instead of the baseline's three wipe-and-rebuild
29	  chains.
30	- Static gate + PASS lines: stages 01–07 all passed first or second try;
31	  the feed-location assertions (user's steering note) held exactly
32	  (PatchBowtie xmax == 45.0 mm).
33	- delete-then-create (ADR 0008): re-runs converged in place repeatedly —
34	  including geometry correction, variable cleanup, and boundary restore.
35	  Wipe-and-rebuild never happened.
36	- Sync-verify runner ultimately printed `PASS: sync replay matches
37	  snapshot` twice — and in doing so exposed **five genuine template bugs**
38	  (below). The machinery works; it was just too noisy th

1	# 08 — Subagent model configurability (one swap point)
2	
3	**What to build:** make the subagents' model assignment changeable in ONE place, so the tier can be re-pointed (e.g. to genuinely cheaper models after the pilot validates the contracts, or to a bigger model if `kb-lookup` proves wrong) without editing agent definitions.
4	
5	Decision context (2026-08-04, supersedes part of grilling Q11): the subagents were originally planned on cheap-tier Fireworks models (~$0.02–0.06/M); the measured cost model shows the dollar delta of that tiering is ~$0.03–0.06 per refactor — negligible. So **both subagents (`kb-lookup`, `runcard`) now run the same `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` at `variant: low` as the main loop**, removing a correctness unknown. Ticket 08 ensures the cheaper tier remains a one-line option later.
6	
7	Implementation: prefer opencode config's env substitution — `"model": "{env:HFSS_SUBAGENT_MODEL}"` on both agents, with the flash ID as the documented default. If env substitution cannot carry the model+variant pair cleanly (verify with `opencode debug config`), fall back to a single provider model alias under `provider.fireworks-ai.models.<alias>` carrying the `variant: low` options, with both agents referencing `fireworks-ai/<alias>` — same property: change the alias's backing model, both agents follow. Document the knob (comment in `opencode.json` + a note in the repo README). The agents' quality contracts are model-incidental: `kb-lookup` must quote-the-KB-or-say-NOT-FOUND, `runcard` caps drafts at ~250 words — the prompts, not the model, carry the behavior.
8	
9	**Status:** ready-for-human

"""Print the opencode run card for a session, from the session database.

Part of the hfss-agent-perf-refactor measurement harness (ticket 01): every
optimization is judged against the numbers this card emits, so the card is
derived from the reference SQL in
docs/hfss-agent-performance-analysis.md section 10.

Wall-time acceptance axis (ticket 11): active wall = Clarification session
start -> the user-gated solver submission instant (solver physics, idle
gaps and post-solve time are out). The start boundary is the ledger's
session-1 "- Started:" line (state.md header block, written once by the
Clarification session); the gate boundary is the machine-state file
results/state/solve_submitted_at.txt (written when the user approves the
solve submission). The card reports raw wall (duration) and active wall
side by side; a missing boundary is reported as "unmeasurable: ...", never
guessed. The verdict-table helper compares active wall only when the
baseline's build-to-solve window is derivable the same way; otherwise the
wall row is marked informational.

The database is opened read-only (WAL-safe while opencode is running) with
a generous busy timeout. Stdlib only, Python 3.10 compatible.

Usage:
    python scripts/run_card.py --slug <slug> [--db PATH] [--workspace DIR]
    python scripts/run_card.py --latest [--db PATH] [--verdict]
    python scripts/run_card.py --slug <slug> --summary <path>/summary.md
    python scripts/run_card.py --latest --summary <path>/summary.md --verdict

--workspace DIR points at a workspace directory (state.md + results/state/);
when --summary is given and --workspace is not, the summary's parent
directory is used. The database path resolves in order: --db flag,
OPENCODE_DB env var, default ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_DB = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "opencode" / "opencode.db"
ENV_DB = "OPENCODE_DB"
PROJECT_MARKER = "HFSS_automation"

1	# HFSS Automation
2	
3	This repo lets a conversation with an agent produce a complete, correct ANSYS HFSS simulation — geometry, materials, excitations, setups, solves, plots, and results. Read `CONTEXT.md` for the domain glossary and `docs/adr/` for settled decisions before working.
4	
5	## Agent skills
6	
7	### Issue tracker
8	
9	Issues and specs live as local markdown under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/` (one spec, one issues/ folder per feature). See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
10	
11	### Triage labels
12	
13	Five canonical labels, each string equal to its name (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`), recorded as `Status:` lines in issue files. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.
14	
15	### Domain docs
16	
17	Single-context: `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root is the domain glossary; decisions live in `docs/adr/`. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.
18	
19	### Fixture fidelity
20	
21	Test fixtures are captured from real artifacts, never written from memory; a synthetic fixture is valid only alongside a real one it provably matches. Two P0 bugs passed a green suite because this was not enforced. See `docs/agents/fixture-fidelity.md`.
22	
23	### Verification tiers
24	
25	`scripts/tier0.py` (seconds, no license) before any AEDT launch; `scripts/tier1.py` builds on the live desktop but never solves; Tier 2 is the full end-to-end run.
26
